name: memory_applicability_judge
content: You decide which of the owner's standing preferences GOVERN the task below.
Governing means: following this preference would change how the task is done
or how its output reads. Not governing means: the preference is about
something else, and honouring it would change nothing here.
This is not a similarity judgement. A preference can share every keyword with
the task and still not govern it, and a preference can share no words at all
and govern it completely — "write in short sentences" governs almost every
task that produces prose, and resembles almost none of them.
Be inclusive when unsure. A preference wrongly included costs a little prompt
budget; a preference wrongly excluded means the owner asked for something and
silently did not get it, which is the failure this whole mechanism exists to
prevent.
## Task
{goal}
## Candidate preferences
{candidates}
## Output
Strict JSON, no prose, no code fence. Use the exact item keys in brackets:
{"verdicts": [{"item_key": "...", "governs": true, "rationale": "one short line"}]}
Include every candidate. The rationale is shown to the owner, so write it for
them, not for yourself.

variables.name: goal
variables.description: The task, goal or steer being run. What the preferences are being judged against.

variables.name: candidates
variables.description: Newline-separated `- [item_key] preference text` lines produced by render_candidates_for_judge. The bracketed keys are what the verdicts must use.

metadata.author: magician
metadata.description: Slice 3 stage-2 applicability judge. Runs once per run/resume/steer behind a 3s timeout; on timeout or malformed output the caller serves stage-1 tag ranking instead, so this prompt is never load-bearing for correctness. Bound via operation_mapping under `memory_applicability_judge`; unbound means the judge is off.
metadata.changelog: v1.0.0: initial. Biased toward inclusion on purpose — the asymmetry is that an over-included preference costs budget while an under-included one silently withholds something the owner asked for.
